items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: And we always had good writers: Sebesky, myself, Ralph Burns, Byers, you know it was great, it was like an education just hanging with those guys.

ctx.x: Well we have to talk about that a little bit. But Manny Albam told me a story about the pressure he was under to do the “West Side Story” record, like it was unbelievable. And you’ve probably had circumstances like that?

A lot, a lot. The most pressures I’ve had, basically one of the things was usually when we write for Liza. That was always a lot of pressure. And we always had good writers: Sebesky, myself, Ralph Burns, Byers, you know it was great, it was like an education just hanging with those guys. But there was always a lot of pressure there because by the time you worked with Liza and you wrote the charts, she has already decided she wants to make changes all over the place. So you’d be running, go over here, you’ve got…

commercial, it’s always the night before. It’s always the dates, you’re writing all night because the date is at nine in the morning. And when I first started doing commercials I would do — this was in the sixties — we would do a spot in the morning. Then in the afternoon, before the spot in the afternoon I would be writing the spot for the morning, the next morning, and then we’d finish the spot after and I’d wind up writing the spot for the —
